name: Kothaparameswarar Temple, Kunnathur
deity: Shiva as Kothaparameswarar, with the Goddess Sivakami
period: Fourth of the Nava Kailasam, the shrine of Rahu; inscriptions show the temple standing by the thirteenth century
summary: On a low hillock at Kunnathur, on the edge of Tirunelveli, Shiva as Kothaparameswarar — his lingam marked with the form of a serpent — keeps the fourth of the Nava Kailasam, the shrine of Rahu.

sections.history: Kunnathur — the village of the hillock — lies on the north-western edge of Tirunelveli, close to Thiruvengadanathapuram, and is also known by its older name Chenkani. The temple of Kothaparameswarar here is the fourth of the Nava Kailasam and the shrine of Rahu, the shadow planet. Its inscriptions show it standing by the thirteenth century, and they name the place Chenkani in Keezh-vembu-nadu, a Vedic settlement called Navaninarayana-chaturvedimangalam. The same records tell of a Pandya king, Veera Pandya, who endowed the temple with money for its daily worship — a gift that set its rituals on a firm footing for generations.
sections.architecture: The temple is a small Dravidian stone shrine set on a gentle rise, which gives the village its name. Its great distinction lies within the sanctum: the lingam of Kothaparameswarar bears the figure of a serpent, a rare feature that devotees connect with Rahu, the serpent-bodied planet, and that makes this the Rahu shrine of the nine. The Goddess Sivakami has her own shrine within the enclosure.
sections.legends: In the Nava Kailasam story, the fourth of the nine lotuses floated down the Tamiraparani by the sage Romasa, disciple of Agastya, came to rest near this hillock, and here he installed the lingam. Local devotion links the serpent-marked lingam to Rahu, and the temple is sought out by those who wish to ease the afflictions astrologers attribute to Rahu and to the serpent powers. With the Vishnu temples of neighbouring Thiruvengadanathapuram, the locality is likened by devotees to the pairing of Kalahasti and Tirupati in the north.
sections.festivals: Maha Shivaratri and the monthly pradosham are kept with devotion, and the Rahu kalam each day — especially on Sundays and Tuesdays — draws devotees seeking relief from Rahu dosha. Confirm dates locally.
sections.experience: Kunnathur is the stop on the Nava Kailasam round closest to Tirunelveli town, and many pilgrims pair it with the Vishnu shrines of Thiruvengadanathapuram nearby. Its small hillside setting and the rare serpent-marked lingam give it a character of its own among the nine.

visit.timings: Open daily with morning and evening darshan sessions and a midday closure; special worship is offered during Rahu kalam. Confirm current timings locally before visiting.
visit.dressCode: Modest traditional dress is expected — shoulders and knees covered; footwear removed before entering. Men are traditionally asked to remove the upper garment before the sanctum, as at many southern shrines; follow the posted rules.
visit.photography: Photography is restricted in and around the sanctum; follow the posted rules and the priests' guidance.
visit.gettingThere: Kunnathur lies in Tirunelveli district near Thiruvengadanathapuram, about 11 km from Tirunelveli Junction; town buses and mini-buses run from Tirunelveli town. Tirunelveli is the nearest railway junction and Thoothukudi the nearest airport.
